findings.summary: The ttl deadline of a new position is deleted in the same timer pass that opened it whenever the terminal does not list the position yet, so the position is never closed at its deadline.
findings.scenario: DoOpen (l.472) stores CM_ttl_<ticket> right after g_trade.Buy/Sell returns. In the same OnTimer call, Watch() (l.396-401) walks the CM_ttl_* variables and does `if(!PositionSelectByTicket(t)) { GlobalVariableDel(gv); continue; }`. If the terminal's list of positions has not yet received the new position when OrderSend returns, the deadline is deleted at once; positions.csv then shows ttl_deadline=0 and nothing ever closes the position (promise 7 and the 'closed even if the brain has stopped' promise). Test O14d (control lag=1) shows it; with --lag the tests O14, O14b and S1 fail for the same reason and nothing else fails.
findings.confidence: Behaviour confirmed by running the real EA code in the imitation (test O14d fails on the original, passes on the corrected copy, also with --lag). The premise is confirmed only in principle: docs page fetched (mql5.com/en/docs/trading/ordersend: 'event(s) of executing trades corresponding to an order may happen after sending a response to the OrderSend() call'). How often the real terminal shows this delay: not verifiable here.

findings.summary: Kill switch, daily lock, starting capital and ttl deadlines are terminal global variables that MetaTrader only writes to disk when it closes normally; after a crash or forced quit they are forgotten.
findings.scenario: The EA never calls GlobalVariablesFlush(). Kill the terminal (SIGKILL in the tests) after the kill switch fired: at restart CM_killed and CM_start do not exist, OnInit (l.609-610) takes the CURRENT balance as starting capital (481.62 instead of 1000) and blocked='' : the 'permanent' stop is gone and -50 % now counts from what is left (test K2). Same for the daily lock: CM_day_bal becomes the current balance, a new daily allowance (test D2: blocked='', day_start_balance=930.12). Same for CM_ttl_*: the position has ttl_deadline=0 after the crash and is never closed (test O14c). A clean restart keeps everything (tests D1, K1, O14b pass).
findings.confidence: Confirmed by execution (tests K2, D2, O14c fail on the original and pass on the corrected copy). Premise confirmed: docs page fetched (mql5.com/en/docs/globals/globalvariablesflush: the terminal 'writes all the global variables when the work is over ... data can be lost at a sudden computer operation failure'). GlobalVariablesFlush was added to check/mql5_shim.h; the corrected copy passes the syntax check.

findings.summary: ttl closes share one 10-second throttle (g_last_close): positions due together are closed 10 s apart, and a position that cannot be closed (its market is closed) keeps the others from being closed at all.
findings.scenario: Watch() l.396-409: for each CM_ttl_* variable past its deadline the test is `now - g_last_close >= 10`, and g_last_close is set to now at the first attempt, so only ONE position is tried per 10 s, always the first one in the loop order. Test O14e: EURUSD, USDJPY and XAUUSD positions with the same ttl; gold cannot be traded (trade mode disabled, as during its daily break). 38 s after the deadline all three are still open: only gold was tried, 4 times; the two positions on open markets were never tried and stay open as long as gold stays closed.
findings.confidence: Confirmed by execution (test O14e fails on the original, passes on the corrected copy). The order in which the real terminal lists global variables (alphabetical in the imitation) is from memory; it only decides WHICH position starves the others, the one-attempt-per-10-s logic is in the code (path read).

findings.summary: On a symbol whose order mode does not include stops in the order, CTrade silently removes the stop: the position is opened WITHOUT a stop and the brain is told ok with sl=4075.23.
findings.scenario: DoOpen calls g_trade.Buy/Sell with sl (l.468). The Standard Library's CTrade::PositionOpen calls OrderTypeCheck, which does `if((flags&SYMBOL_ORDER_SL)==0) m_request.sl=0.0;` before sending. The EA never checks SYMBOL_ORDER_MODE nor the stop of the resulting position. Test O19 (symbol XAUUSD.r with SYMBOL_ORDER_MODE lacking SYMBOL_ORDER_SL): answer ok=True, sl=4075.23, while the broker's position has sl=0. Promise 1 ('aucun ordre sans stop; le stop est pose chez le courtier') is broken on such a symbol.
findings.confidence: Confirmed: code path read in the real Trade.mqh (Copyright 2000-2025) kept in the repository, lab/audit/scratch/mql5_v21/compile_api/ref_trade_mqh/T.mqh lines 1599-1650 (OrderTypeCheck), transcribed in mock_mains.h, and executed (test O19 fails on the original, passes on the corrected copy). Whether any of the six FP Markets symbols lacks SYMBOL_ORDER_SL: unknown (unlikely for CFDs, cannot be checked here). SYMBOL_ORDER_MODE / SYMBOL_ORDER_SL were added to check/mql5_shim.h.

findings.summary: 'nan' in sl, tp or volume passes every check of the hands: an open goes to the broker with the full requested volume and a NaN stop, a modify goes to the broker with a NaN stop, and volume=nan opens the largest volume the risk cap allows.
findings.scenario: pont.py writes sl=repr(float(sl)) and volume=f'{volume:.4f}', so a NaN computed by the brain (missing data in an indicator) arrives as 'sl=nan' / 'volume=nan'. In DoOpen every comparison with NaN is false: `sl <= 0` (l.446) no, wrong side (l.447) no, `r1 <= 0` (l.453) no; cap / r1 is NaN so the cap no longer limits the volume (l.455) and Buy is called with volume=0.05 (the full request) and sl=nan. Test O18: the request 'open XAUUSD.r volume=0.05 sl=nan' reaches the trade server; only the broker's own validation can still refuse. With volume=nan and a valid stop the position IS opened (0.02 lot, the cap). In DoModify (l.502-509) sl=nan passes 'stop obligatoire' and the direction check and is sent to the broker. Related, cosmetic (H12): a volume of 0, unreadable or under the minimum lot is refused with 'limite de risque : le lot minimum (0.01) risquerait 4.31, limite 10.00', a message that contradicts itself.
findings.confidence: Confirmed by execution in the imitation (test O18 fails on the original, passes on the corrected copy), where StringToDouble is C's strtod and so reads 'nan'/'inf'. Whether the real MQL5 StringToDouble("nan") returns NaN: from memory (I believe (double)"nan" gives NaN in MQL5), not verified. What pont.py writes for a NaN: confirmed by reading pont.py lines 182-184. MathIsValidNumber was added to check/mql5_shim.h.

findings.summary: On a market whose lot step is not a power of ten (0.5, 0.25, 0.05) the volume is rounded after the risk cap was applied: with step 0.5 it is rounded UP to twice the allowed size.
findings.scenario: l.456 computes vd = round(-log10(vstep)) and l.457 does NormalizeDouble(floor(vol/vstep)*vstep, vd). With vstep=0.5: vd=0, so 0.5 becomes 1.0. Test O17 (NAS100 with step and minimum 0.5, stop 15.00 away, cap 10 EUR): 0.5 lot is allowed (6.47 EUR at risk), 1.0 lot is opened, risk_money=12.94 for a cap of 10.00. With step 0.25 or 0.05 the result (0.3, 0.2...) is not a multiple of the step: the server refuses every order (invalid volume) or the size is rounded up. Steps 0.01 and 0.1 are correct (test O7 on five markets).
findings.fix:
OLD (lines 456-457):
   int vd = (int)MathMax(0, MathMin(4, MathRound(-MathLog10(vstep))));
   vol = NormalizeDouble(MathFloor(vol / vstep + 1e-9) * vstep, vd);    // taille reduite d'office a la limite de risque
NEW:
   vol = NormalizeDouble(MathFloor(vol / vstep + 1e-9) * vstep, 8);     // taille reduite d'office a la limite de risque (multiple exact du pas, jamais arrondie vers le haut)
findings.confidence: Confirmed by execution (test O17 fails on the original, passes on the corrected copy), with a lot step set through the control file. That MQL5's NormalizeDouble(0.5, 0) gives 1.0 (round half away from zero): from memory. The real lot steps of FP Markets' six symbols are unknown here; if they are all 0.01 / 0.1 / 1 the defect never shows.

findings.summary: The order file is moved to done/ only AFTER execution and the result of FileMove is ignored: if the move fails the same order is executed again on every timer pass.
findings.scenario: RunCommand executes (l.522-527), writes the answer (l.528), then FileMove(path, 0, DIR + "done\\" + file, FILE_REWRITE) at l.530 without looking at its result. Test R10: the done folder was removed (a user tidying the bridge folder); one 'open' sent through pont.py; 2 positions are opened (until 'trop de positions sur ce marche'), the file stays in cmd/ and is run again on every pass, each time rewriting the answer and every export. For a stuck close_all, every later position of the robot would be closed as soon as it is opened. Not run but same root: the EA attached to two charts by mistake (both instances read the file before either moves it), or a terminal crash between execution and the move (the order is executed again at restart, test R4 shows orders left in cmd/ are executed).
findings.confidence: Confirmed by execution (test R10 fails on the original, passes on the corrected copy; R1, R4, R9, R11 still pass with the correction). In the imitation FileMove into a missing folder fails (POSIX rename); whether the real FileMove fails or creates the folder: unknown, not verified. The two-instances scenario was not run (the imitation's broker is per process).

findings.summary: If the server clock steps back (the hour gained when the broker's clock leaves US summer time, a clock correction), account.txt / positions.csv stop being rewritten and forced closes stop being retried until the clock has caught up (up to an hour).
findings.scenario: l.634 `now - g_last_fast >= 5` and l.390 / l.402 `now - g_last_close >= 10` are negative after a step back. Test R12: server clock set back 3600 s; 8 s later account.txt is 8 s old and will stay so for an hour unless a trade happens; pont.ea_alive() (30 s) then says the hands are dead, and a Friday close / kill-switch close that failed just before is not retried.
findings.fix:
OLD (line 390):
   if(flat && CountPositions() > 0 && now - g_last_close >= 10)        // on insiste toutes les 10 s tant qu'il reste une position
NEW:

OLD (line 634):

NEW:
   if(g_dirty || now - g_last_fast >= 5 || now < g_last_fast)          // (now < ... : l'horloge du serveur a recule)
(line 402 is covered by the replacement given in H14, whose `due` already contains `|| now < g_last_close`)
findings.confidence: The EA's behaviour is confirmed by execution (test R12 fails on the original, passes on the corrected copy). That TimeTradeServer() of the real terminal can step back (server offset change on the US clock change, on a Sunday; clock corrections): from memory, not verified.

findings.summary: A modify that changes nothing (same stop, same target) is answered ok=0 'refuse par le serveur : 10025 no changes'.
findings.scenario: DoModify l.509 sends the request even when sl and tp equal the current values. The server answers 10025 and OrderSend returns false, so Done() (l.415-419) returns false although it lists TRADE_RETCODE_NO_CHANGES (that branch can never be reached through `ok &&`). Test M4: h.modify(ticket, sl=4075.23, tp=4100.0) on a position that already has them -> ok=False. A brain that re-sends its stop every cycle sees refusals.

That the real OrderSend returns false with retcode 10025 for an unchanged SL/TP request: from memory, not verified (the documentation page fetched does not say). The correction does not depend on it: nothing is sent when nothing changes.

findings.summary: A requested volume of 0, unreadable, negative or under the minimum lot is refused with a risk-limit message that contradicts itself.
findings.scenario: l.455-460: vol becomes 0, `vol < vmin` is true and the reason is built from r1 * vmin. Test R8 (volume 'abc', '', '-1', '0', '0.004' with a stop 5.00 away): reason 'limite de risque : le lot minimum (0.01) risquerait 4.31, limite 10.00' (4.31 is under the limit). Refusing is right; the brain's log gets a wrong reason.

limitations: MetaEditor has still never compiled ClaudeMains.mq5: only g++ on the translation has (syntax check and now a full build + run). The first build in MetaEditor remains the real test, also for the proposed corrections (they pass the same g++ check; GlobalVariablesFlush, MathIsValidNumber, SYMBOL_ORDER_MODE / SYMBOL_ORDER_SL were added to mql5_shim.h from memory of the documentation).

The symbols are invented (names XAUUSD.r / NAS100 / BTCUSD / ETHUSD / EURUSD.r / USDJPY.r, lot sizes, steps, stops level, tick values in EUR, leverage, commission and fee). Timing: the imitation calls OnTimer every 15 ms and delivers OnTradeTransaction right after each handler; the real terminal fires the timer once a second, OrderSend blocks for the network round trip, and the list of positions / history is refreshed at an unknown moment. The lag=1 mode is a worst case built from the documentation's wording, not a measurement.

The trade server is a simple model: fills at the current bid/ask, SL/TP filled at the scripted price, OrderSend returns false for every failing retcode (true only with ordersend_true=1). Real behaviour not covered: partial fills, requotes and price deviation, retcode 10008 'placed' with no deal and no price yet (the EA would then report price=0 / volume=0 to the brain), stop-out by the broker, swaps, the hedged-margin rules, SYMBOL_FILLING modes other than FOK/IOC.

File sharing between MetaTrader under Wine and Python on macOS is not reproduced: locks, FileMove onto a file Python has open, FileMove into a missing folder, whether FileOpen fails on a file being written. FileReadString on LF-only files: the documentation (page fetched) only promises lines ended by CRLF; test R7 shows both outcomes; pont.py writes CRLF.

Clocks: TimeGMT() is the machine's clock and TimeTradeServer() is that clock plus an offset set by the test. Whether the real terminal's TimeGMT() under Wine equals the Mac's time.time() (brain timeout, pont.ea_alive) and how TimeTradeServer() behaves when disconnected or at a clock change cannot be shown here.

Global variables: persistence is modelled from the documentation (saved at a normal close and on GlobalVariablesFlush); the order of GlobalVariableName(), the 4-week expiry and the behaviour of the real terminal at a forced quit on macOS are not verified.

The margin mode is read at each call here, whereas the real CTrade reads it once in its constructor (a global object, built before OnInit): if the account is not loaded at that moment the real PositionClosePartial would refuse; not modelled.

The premise of finding H13 (balance and equity read 0 before the terminal is connected) and the NaN parsing of StringToDouble (H4), the NormalizeDouble(0.5, 0) = 1.0 rounding (H3), OrderSend returning false on 10025 (H10) and a server clock stepping back (H11) are assumptions from memory built into the imitation or the tests; they are marked as such in each finding.

Only one EA instance on one chart is run. Two instances on the same bridge folder, a second EA with the same magic number, a change of account, and chart re-initialisation (timeframe change calling OnInit again) were not run.

harness.summary:
The real code of ClaudeMains.mq5 now runs here: translated by to_cpp.py, linked with a working imitation of the terminal and broker (check/mock_mains.h, which includes main()), and driven only through pont.py's Hands plus a control file (check/test_mains.py).

Final runs, all from /home/user/gold-orb:
- **test_mains.py**: 60 tests, 45 pass, 0 fail, 15 expected failures (each tied to a finding), exit 0. The result was the same in five consecutive runs and at -j 1, 6 and 12.
- **test_releve.py**: "ReleveFP : tous les tests passent", exit 0.
- **test_pont.py**: "pont : tous les tests passent", exit 0.
- **Syntax checks**: both ClaudeMains and ReleveFP (with `-include check/mql5_shim.h`) exit 0 with no warning.

How far the suite can be trusted:
- **Mutation check**: 28 deliberate breakages of the EA in scratch copies (no stop check, magic filter removed, risk cap doubled, Friday off, and so on) were all caught.
- **Sanitizers**: one full run under address and undefined-behaviour sanitizers gave the same result with no report.
- **Late position list (`--lag`)**: only the ttl tests fail on the original, all from finding H1.

Promises kept in the imitation (tests pass):
- **Exports**: every export parses through pont.py, including the missing-market row, the fee column, deals rewritten after each transaction and once a minute, completed bars only, and UTC conversion at +2 h and +3 h.
- **Open**: every listed refusal works, and the risk cap is correct on five markets with lot steps 0.01 and 0.1.
- **Modify, close, partial close, close_all**: all behave as promised.
- **Positions opened by hand or by another robot**: never touched by close, modify, close_all, the Friday close, the daily lock or the kill switch.
- **Silent brain, daily loss lock, kill switch, Friday close and weekend block**: all hold, including across a normal restart and with InpResetLocks for the kill switch.

Promises not kept (14 findings, each with a failing test except H12, which is the misleading message printed by test R8):
- **Maximum position lifetime**:
  - H1: the deadline is deleted if the terminal lists the new position late.
  - H2: the deadline, the kill switch, the daily lock and the starting capital are lost if the terminal crashes.
  - H14: one position that cannot be closed keeps the others from being closed.
- **Stop and risk cap**:
  - H5: CTrade silently drops the stop on a symbol that does not take one in the order.
  - H4: "nan" in sl or volume passes every check; pont.py does write "nan" if the brain computes one.
  - H3: with a lot step of 0.5 the volume is rounded up to twice the cap.
- **Orders and answers**:
  - H8: an order is re-executed on every pass if its file cannot be moved to done/.
  - H6: close_all answers ok when closes failed.
  - H7: a comma in the tag breaks positions.csv and deals.csv for pont.py.
  - H10: a modify that changes nothing is reported as a refusal.
  - H12: a zero or unreadable volume is refused with a wrong reason.
- **Locks and clock**:
  - H9: InpResetLocks does not lift the daily lock.
  - H11: a server clock stepping back stalls account.txt and close retries.
  - H13: a false permanent stop if the account reads 0 before connection; this premise is unverified.

All proposed replacements were applied together to a scratch copy (never to the repository file). That copy passes the syntax check and the whole suite: 45 pass and the 15 expected failures now pass, also with `--lag`.

Observations that are not defects, printed as notes by the tests:
- **Half-written order file (R2)**: it can execute without ttl or expire, though never above the cap or without a stop; pont.py writes atomically.
- **Duplicate id (R3)**: the order is executed again; pont.py never reuses ids.
- **Orders left in cmd/ across a restart (R4)**: `expire` is honoured and they run in id order; anything without `expire` (close, modify, close_all, a raw open) is executed late.
- **InpStartBalance > 0 (K3)**: InpResetLocks cannot lift the kill switch while funds are under half of it.

findings.summary: The kill switch, the daily lock, the start capital and the TTL deadlines are kept in terminal global variables, and MT5 only writes those to disk when the terminal stops normally. If MT5/Wine on macOS crashes or is force-quit, CM_killed and CM_day_lock come back as 0 and the hard limits 5 and 6 are lifted.
findings.scenario: Watch() line 380 sets CM_killed=1 (or line 386 sets CM_day_lock=1) and CloseAll runs. The Mac then sleeps, crashes or the user force-quits MetaTrader. On restart OnInit line 611 sees no CM_killed (GlobalVariableCheck false) and sets it to 0.0, so Blocked() returns "" and new positions are accepted again. CM_ttl_<ticket> deadlines set at line 472 are lost the same way, so the max-duration rule stops applying. The mock models the same thing (mock_mains.h line 25: saved 'on GlobalVariablesFlush() and at a clean exit only').
findings.confidence: confirmed (docs page globals/globalvariablesflush fetched: 'The terminal writes all the global variables when the work is over ... data can be lost at a sudden computer operation failure'). Whether a Wine crash on macOS counts as 'sudden failure' is from memory, not tested.

findings.summary: InpSlippagePts (SetDeviationInPoints) is not a hard limit on a Market Execution symbol, which is what FP Markets uses. The fill can be worse than the quote used for the risk calculation, so the real risk can go above InpMaxRiskPct while risk_money reports the risk at the quote.
findings.scenario: DoOpen sizes vol from price = tk.ask/tk.bid (lines 443, 452-457) and then calls Buy(vol, nm, 0.0, sl, tp, cm). Under SYMBOL_TRADE_EXECUTION_MARKET the deviation field is not part of the request the server honours, so a news spike on XAUUSD fills N points further away. The loss at the stop is then |fill - sl|/ts*tv*vol > cap, while line 474 reports risk_money = r1*vol computed at the old quote.
findings.confidence: from memory (deviation ignored under Market Execution). Partly backed by the docs page structures/mqltraderequest (fetched): for Market Execution the required fields are action, symbol, volume, type, type_filling, and deviation is listed only for Instant Execution. FP Markets' execution mode is from memory; ReleveFP.mq5 exports SYMBOL_TRADE_EXEMODE, so the survey's output would confirm it.

EURUSD buy and XAUUSD sell both with ttl 10 min; at the deadline gold is in its daily break (broker answers 10018). 88 s later: 9 attempts on gold, 0 on EURUSD, both still open; EURUSD stays open until gold reopens (an hour on a normal night, the whole week-end otherwise).

By reading, lines 380, 386 and 472 only call GlobalVariableSet, with no flush anywhere. Harness D2, K2 and O14c are XFAIL on the unmodified file in my run, but that is the mock's model of the terminal. The fix is INCOMPLETE. CM_day and CM_day_bal are set at the start of each day (lines 373-375) and never flushed. After a crash later that day without a lock (for example at -5 %), the restart sees an old CM_day, treats it as a new day, and takes the remaining balance as the new baseline: the 5 % already lost is forgotten. L6's DayBaseline would also cover this.
verdicts.fix:
As proposed (KILL_FILE plus GlobalVariablesFlush after lines 380, 386 and 472, FileDelete in the InpResetLocks block, restore after line 612, flush at the end of OnInit). ALSO, inside the new-day block, after line 375 (GlobalVariableSet("CM_day_lock", 0.0);) add:
      GlobalVariablesFlush();                                           // le solde du debut de journee survit a un plantage

verdicts.reason: The code path is real by reading. OnInit calls Watch() at line 614. With eq = 0, line 378 trips the kill switch, line 384 the daily lock, and line 610 stores CM_start = 0, which disables 'start > 0'. The finding stands or falls on its premise: that AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE/EQUITY) returns 0 before the terminal is connected. The docs do not say so, I could not test it on a terminal, and the harness K4 marks it as an assumption too. Related doc fact: REASON_ACCOUNT also covers a reconnection to the trade server, so OnInit can run again at that moment. The suggested guard ('if(TerminalInfoInteger(TERMINAL_CONNECTED) == 0 || bal <= 0) return;' at the top of Watch, plus re-seeding CM_start when <= 0) is harmless and cheap to apply anyway. What is missing is one run on the real terminal, started with the EA already on a chart.

Confirmed by reading lines 371-376. The baseline is the balance at the hands' first Watch() of the server day, and deposits and withdrawals move it. Reviewer's adv.py on the unmodified file: a7 day_start 939.96 after losses at 03:00; a6 blocked='' after -10.4 %; a6b false lock after a 100 withdrawal. I checked the fix by reading. DayBaseline subtracts only BUY/SELL deal profit + swap + commission + fee for today (DEAL_FEE is already used at line 329). With history not yet loaded it falls back to bal, and the once-a-minute recomputation then corrects itself. It does not change how a position held over midnight is counted compared with today's code. How FP books commission on deals is not verified.
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading lines 603-608: the reset runs on every OnInit while the input is true. The official uninit-reason page lists REASON_CHARTCHANGE ('Symbol or chart period has been changed'), REASON_PARAMETERS, REASON_ACCOUNT (includes a reconnection to the trade server) and REASON_CLOSE. Each is followed by a new OnInit for an EA still on the chart, so the kill is cleared again at each of those events. Reviewer's adv.py a4 on the unmodified file: start 222.61, blocked=''. I checked the fix by reading. CM_reset_used gives one reset per false->true change, which keeps the header's 'true UNE fois'. It needs L11's flush at the end of OnInit to survive a crash.
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading a MetaQuotes Trade.mqh copy (header 'Copyright 2000-2025', in the scratchpad's trade_mqh/t.mqh; where it came from was not checked). CTrade::PositionOpen (line 303) calls OrderTypeCheck, and that function at lines 1640-1641 does 'if((flags&SYMBOL_ORDER_SL)==0) m_request.sl=0.0;' and still returns true. DoOpen then answers ok=1 with sl=... (line 474). Nothing in Watch() looks at POSITION_SL. DoModify skips the 'only closer' test when cur_sl == 0 (line 507). Harness O19 is XFAIL and adv.py a12 shows the modify accepted on the unmodified file. Nuance: a far stop on a position with no stop is still less risk than no stop at all. The real gap is the naked position, which the proposed sweep closes. Whether any FP symbol lacks SYMBOL_ORDER_SL is unknown (unlikely). The fix is correct by reading.
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading lines 520-530. The order runs, then res is written, then FileMove's result is ignored, so a file that cannot be moved runs again every second. ReadKV opens with FILE_SHARE_READ (line 75), so two instances on two charts can both read and run the same file. Harness R10 is XFAIL on the unmodified file. Scenario (2) is mostly harmless: pont always sends expire, so a replayed open is refused as 'ordre perime', and a replayed close of a closed ticket gives 'position introuvable'. A replayed partial close would still close twice. Fix checked by reading: renaming is atomic, so with two instances only one FileMove succeeds and the other returns without running the order. Other side effects of two instances remain (doubled exports and closes). A one-instance guard would be a separate change.
verdicts.fix: As proposed (requires L2's bool return; otherwise 'return;').

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by arithmetic and reading lines 456-457. vd = round(-log10(step)) gives 0 for step 0.5 and 1 for steps 0.05 and 0.25 (I checked in Python). NormalizeDouble to those digits moves 0.5 to the nearest whole lot, 0.05 to 0.1 and 0.25 to 0.3, i.e. above the floor-to-step value. Harness O17 is XFAIL on the unmodified file. FP's real lot steps are unknown (COSTS_FP.md open question 1). Normalizing to 8 digits keeps the floor-to-step value. The fix is correct.
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading. Line 525 ignores what CloseAll did (CloseAll is void and only Prints). Line 390 retries every 10 s while FridayClosed(now) holds on Saturday and Sunday. No Notify on any failed forced close. Harness C4 XFAIL; adv.py a10 shows 12 requests per 120 s on the unmodified file. The fix is correct by reading. It relies on signed datetime differences (now - (now+50)), which the doc's __time64_t analogue supports. With L5 corrected to use g_next_ttl, the +50 on g_last_close no longer interacts with the ttl loop.
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading lines 186-192 and 389. The weekend close happens only while FridayClosed() holds (Fri >= 23:50 to Sun 24:00 server time) and MT5 is running; from Monday nothing retries. I checked the calendar with Python: 2026-11-27, 2026-12-25 and 2027-01-01 are Fridays. Early or full closures on those days are from memory, not checked with FP. The fix (documentation plus the L8 alert) is honest and correct. A possible code addition, not required: in Watch(), close any robot position whose POSITION_TIME is earlier than the last Friday-close time. This at least ends a position that was carried over a weekend by accident, at the first open market.
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading lines 548-552: the cut at 100 happens before the sort. The docs do not promise any order for FileFindFirst/Next. adv.py a15 on the unmodified file leaves 1 position open, but only because the mock lists names in reverse on purpose. Real listing order on MT5 for macOS is unverified. Practically hard to reach: pont.send is synchronous and deletes its file on timeout, so more than 100 pending files needs another writer. The fix is a correct partial selection sort by reading (the 100 smallest of up to 5000, in order).
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

verdicts.reason: The code path holds only if MQL5's StringToDouble("nan") returns NaN. The official StringToDouble page says nothing about invalid strings or nan/inf, and I could not run MQL5. If it returns 0, line 446 already refuses the order. The harness O18 result comes from the mock's own StringToDouble, so it proves nothing about MQL5. What is missing is one compile-and-run in MetaEditor (Print(StringToDouble("nan"))). Cheap safeguards that cost nothing: the proposed MathIsValidNumber checks (the function is declared in the shim and exists in MQL5, from memory), or on the brain side, refuse non-finite volume/sl/tp in pont.open/modify before writing the file.

Confirmed by reading. Line 439 accepts any tick with positive bid and ask, whatever its age. Lines 452-457 size on tk.ask, and lines 473-474 report r1 * vol computed BEFORE the fill, so the brain never learns the risk at the actual fill price. That market execution ignores the deviation is from memory; the MqlTradeRequest page I fetched lists only action, symbol, volume, type, type_filling as required and is silent on deviation. Normal slippage is enough to exceed the cap with a tight stop (COSTS_FP.md models 1 bp on gold stop fills = 0.41 USD, +31 % on a 1.30 USD stop), and L1 bounds that. The proposed check is WEAK: the official TimeCurrent page says it is 'the time of the last quote receipt for one of the symbols', so it stops moving when the whole feed pauses and the check then passes. TimeTradeServer() keeps advancing. I syntax-checked and ran the corrected line in the mock (no harness change).

Confirmed by reading. Hands.send waits 20 s (lines 125-143), then deletes the cmd file. expire = server_time from account.txt + 20 (line 156), and the EA accepts while TimeTradeServer() <= expire (line 437), then blocks in OrderSend before writing res. A pickup shortly before the 20 s mark plus a slow OrderSend gives a fill after the brain has returned 'pas de réponse'. The window is narrow: account.txt is up to 5 s old, which shortens expire. It was not reproduced (the mock fills instantly). I applied the replacement to a scratch copy of pont.py: test_pont.py passes. The same race exists for close/modify/close_all, which have no expire; the brain should re-read positions() after any 'pas de réponse'.
verdicts.fix: As proposed (timeout=valid_sec + 15 on open, and the brain re-reads positions() after any 'pas de réponse').

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading. There is no FileDelete anywhere in ClaudeMains.mq5, and pont.py deletes cmd/<id>.txt only on timeout. The proposed fix is INCOMPLETE: the EA writes res\<id>.txt (line 528) BEFORE it moves the order to done\ (line 530). The brain polls every 0.2 s and can see res while the file is still in cmd\, so unlink of done/<id>.txt fails silently and that file stays. Corrected: also unlink cmd/<id>.txt. If the EA has not moved it yet, its later FileMove just fails, harmlessly, since it already ran. If L7 is applied, done\ exists before res and the race disappears. Answers to timed-out sends are still never removed. I applied the corrected version to a scratch copy: test_pont.py passes.
verdicts.fix:
pont.py, in send(), before 'return r' (line 142):
                for sub in ("res", "done", "cmd"):          # réponse lue : on ne laisse pas res/ et done/ grossir sans fin
                    try:                                   # (cmd/ aussi : les mains écrivent res/ AVANT de déplacer l'ordre)
                        (self.dir / sub / f"{cid}.txt").unlink()
                    except OSError:
                        pass
                return r
Harness R9 (asserts done/<id>.txt exists) must be adapted.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed by reading. Every robot filter is 'POSITION_MAGIC != InpMagic' (lines 161, 295, 358, 481, 495), so InpMagic = 0 matches positions opened by hand, which have magic 0 (from memory). Line 472 stores the ttl under ResultOrder(), which on a netting account is not the position ticket after a second open. The EventSetTimer result is ignored at line 613. Low severity: the defaults (magic 20261110, hedging account) do not trigger it. I applied the exact replacement to a copy and checked it: to_cpp.py + g++ -fsyntax-only passes against the shim (Alert, INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT, ACCOUNT_LOGIN, ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE and bool EventSetTimer are declared there). MetaEditor was not run.
verdicts.fix: As proposed.

steps.action: Brancher le Mac sur secteur et noter la version de macOS (menu Pomme > À propos de ce Mac).
steps.detail: The current MetaQuotes installer (bundle 5.0.6275, dated 2026-10-20) declares LSMinimumSystemVersion 12 (Monterey). Confirmed by unpacking the .pkg's Info.plist. The help page still says Catalina 10.15.7, which is out of date. If the Mac runs macOS Tahoe 26.x, warn the lead: MQL5 forum threads from May to July 2026 report random MT5 crashes on Tahoe 26.5, often while placing or closing orders (see pitfalls).

steps.action: Empêcher la mise en veille : Réglages Système > Batterie > Options > activer « Empêcher la suspension automatique sur adaptateur secteur lorsque l'écran est éteint ». Garder l'écran du portable ouvert.
steps.detail: While the Mac sleeps every process is suspended, so the EA, the Python brain and Remote Control all stop. That is from memory as general macOS behaviour; a vendor guide says the same for MT5. Apple documents this setting under Battery > Options; older macOS versions put it under Energy Saver or Displays > Advanced. A laptop sleeps when the lid closes unless it is in clamshell mode (external display, power and keyboard); from memory. 'caffeinate' or the Claude app's keep-awake switch block idle sleep. From memory, they do not reliably block sleep when the lid closes.

steps.action: Télécharger MetaTrader 5 pour Mac depuis https://www.metatrader5.com/en/download (bouton macOS), PAS depuis le lien de la page d'aide.
steps.detail: Confirmed by downloading both files. The download page links https://download.terminal.free/cdn/web/metaquotes.ltd/mt5/MetaTrader5.pkg.zip: 506 MB, pkg dated 2026-10-20, bundled Wine 11.7. The help page install_mac still links .../metaquotes.software.corp/mt5/MetaTrader5.pkg.zip: 480 MB, dated 2025-02-14, Wine 10.0. A MetaQuotes moderator recommends Wine 11.3 or later on recent macOS. I found no FP Markets-branded Mac installer: fpmarkets.com returns 403 to automated clients, and guessed CDN names such as /cdn/web/22955/mt5/fpmarketssc5.pkg.zip return 404, while the FP Windows installer does exist. Using the generic MetaQuotes build and searching for the broker inside it is the documented path.

steps.action: Double-cliquer le fichier téléchargé, suivre l'installateur, accepter l'installation de Mono et Gecko (et de Rosetta si le Mac le demande).
steps.detail: The pkg installs '/Applications/MetaTrader 5.app' (bundle id net.metaquotes.wine.MetaTrader5). Its postinstall runs the app with --install to build the Wine prefix, then launches it and opens mql5.com in the browser. Confirmed by reading the pkg's postinstall script. The help page says the Mono and Gecko prompts must be accepted. From memory: Apple Silicon needs Rosetta 2 because the Wine binaries are x86_64, and macOS offers to install it. The app is not sandboxed (com.apple.security.app-sandbox = false, confirmed from the embedded entitlements), so its data sits in plain ~/Library/Application Support and not in a container. The interface language follows the macOS language at install time.

steps.action: Ouvrir le compte démo FP Markets : de préférence depuis l'espace client FP Markets (Client Portal) ; sinon dans MT5 : Fichier > Ouvrir un compte, taper « FP Markets », choisir le serveur « …-Demo », cocher « Utiliser la couverture (hedge) », dépôt 1000 EUR, levier 1:500.
steps.detail: The MT5 help confirms the File > Open an Account flow: search for the broker, choose a demo account, tick 'Use hedge in trading' (otherwise the account is netting), pick deposit and leverage from the broker's lists. Server names confirmed from FP Markets' own demo web terminals: FPMarketsSC-Demo (Seychelles entity, mt5demowebtradersc.fpmarkets.com) and FPMarkets-Demo (Australian entity, mt5demowebtraderau.fpmarkets.com). The server must match the entity of the user's FP account; 1:500 points to the non-EU (SC) entity. Not verified: whether FP allows demo registration from inside the terminal, and whether a Raw demo type is offered there. The client portal email gives login, password and server, and a third-party guide warns not to confuse the portal password with the MT5 password.

steps.action: Se connecter (Fichier > Se connecter au compte de trading), puis ouvrir la Boîte à outils (Affichage > Boîte à outils) onglet « Journal » et lire les premières lignes à voix haute au responsable.
steps.detail: The startup lines show the build, the Windows version, 'on Wine X.Y Darwin ...' and the data path. A forum log from Aug 2026 shows 'Terminal C:\Program Files\MetaTrader 5'. Expect Wine 11.x. If it shows Wine 8 or 10, MetaQuotes advises uninstalling: move the app to the Trash and delete ~/Library/Application Support/net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5 and ~/Library/Application Support/Metatrader 5. Then reinstall from step 3. Also confirm the account is a demo, in hedging mode and in EUR.

steps.action: Ouvrir la fenêtre Symboles (Affichage > Symboles) et lire au responsable les noms exacts de l'or, du Nasdaq, du Bitcoin (ex. XAUUSD.r ou XAUUSD, US100 ou NAS100).
steps.detail: FP Markets' FAQ (via search snippet, an old page) says Raw symbols on the FPMarkets-live server end in '.r', and that live2 shows no suffix. I could not confirm the naming on FPMarketsSC-Demo. Index and crypto names (US100, JP225, BTCUSD, ETHUSD) are from memory and the repo's earlier sweeps (lab/COSTS_FP.md), not verified on FP's site. ClaudeMains and ReleveFP find the suffix themselves; the lead should check symbols.csv and tous.csv afterwards.
steps.source: https://www.fpmarkets.com/education/faq/ (403 to automated fetch; content from search snippet only)

steps.action: Copier les fichiers : dans le Finder, menu Aller > Aller au dossier… (Maj-Cmd-G), coller ~/Library/Application Support/net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5/drive_c/Program Files/MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Experts puis y glisser ClaudeMains.mq5 ; même chose avec …/MQL5/Scripts pour ReleveFP.mq5.
steps.detail: The path is confirmed four ways: the official help page; the launcher binary contains 'net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5' and 'C:\Program Files\MetaTrader 5\terminal64.exe'; the installer payload ships 'MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Experts', 'Scripts' and 'Include/Trade/Trade.mqh'; a 2025-09 forum user found it there. The data folder is the install folder: no AppData/<hash> folder, because Wine runs as admin. MQL5/Files does not exist until a program writes there. Avoid File > Open Data Folder: on the Mac it opens a Wine Explorer window, and users report that paste fails or the command only beeps (forum reports from 2023 to 2025). Pasting via right-click in that window works for some users. Finder 'Go to Folder' is the dependable route. ~/Library is hidden in Finder; 'Go to Folder' bypasses that.

steps.action: Ouvrir MetaEditor (menu Outils > MetaQuotes Language Editor), dans son Navigateur ouvrir Experts > ClaudeMains.mq5, cliquer le bouton « Compiler » ; lire l'onglet « Erreurs » (doit finir par 0 errors). Recommencer avec Scripts > ReleveFP.mq5.
steps.detail: MetaEditor is bundled: metaeditor64.exe is in the payload of both the 2025 and the 2026 installers (confirmed). Compile = File > Compile or F7; results go to the Errors tab, and no .ex5 is produced if there are errors (official MetaEditor help). On a Mac keyboard F7 is usually a media key, so press fn+F7 or use the toolbar button (from memory). From memory, shortcuts inside the Wine windows use Ctrl, not Cmd. If the new files don't appear, right-click the Navigator and choose Refresh. Have the user read out or screenshot any error lines: this is the first real MetaEditor compile of ClaudeMains.

steps.action: Lancer d'abord le script ReleveFP : dans MT5, Navigateur > Scripts > ReleveFP, le glisser sur n'importe quel graphique, OK ; attendre le message de fin (fini.txt).
steps.detail: It writes claude/releve/*.csv and uses CopyTicksRange. The Mac terminal is the same Windows terminal64.exe under Wine (confirmed from the payload), so CopyTicksRange is expected to behave as on Windows; I found no Mac-specific source for that. Tick depth depends on FP's server. ReleveFP writes its final files in place, with no tmp file and rename, so nobody should read them before fini.txt appears.

steps.action: Activer le trading algorithmique : bouton « Algo Trading » de la barre d'outils (il doit devenir vert) et Outils > Options > Expert Advisors > « Autoriser le trading algorithmique ».
steps.detail: The help pages still call it 'AutoTrading' / 'Allow Auto Trading'. Current MT5 builds label it 'Algo Trading' / 'Allow Algo Trading' (forum and memory). Without it EAs run but cannot trade. Leave 'Disable automated trading when switching accounts' as it is, and DLL imports off; ClaudeMains needs no DLL.

steps.action: Attacher ClaudeMains : Navigateur > Expert Advisors > ClaudeMains, le glisser sur un graphique (ex. XAUUSD M5) ; onglet Commun : cocher « Autoriser le trading algo » ; onglet Paramètres : ne rien changer sauf consigne ; OK.
steps.detail: Official help: double-click or drag from the Navigator, the properties window opens, and on success the EA name and icon appear in the chart's top-right corner. Without a brain the EA opens nothing new (limit 7). Only one chart should run ClaudeMains.

steps.action: Vérifier : Boîte à outils > onglet « Experts » (messages de ClaudeMains) ; puis dans le Finder, Aller au dossier …/MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Files/claude et vérifier qu'account.txt, symbols.csv, bars_*.csv apparaissent.
steps.detail: The Experts tab shows EA messages. The same logs are on disk under …/MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Logs/yyyymmdd.log and terminal logs under …/MetaTrader 5/Logs (official Files and Folders page).

steps.action: Notifications : installer l'appli MetaTrader 5 sur le téléphone, y lire le MetaQuotes ID (Messages / Réglages), puis dans MT5 Mac : Outils > Options > Notifications, cocher « Activer les notifications push », coller l'ID, cliquer Tester.
steps.detail: Official help: the recipient is identified by the MetaQuotes ID shown in the mobile app's Messages section; up to 4 IDs can be entered, separated by commas. The EA's SendNotification only works once this is set up. Nothing Mac-specific was found.

steps.action: Installer Python depuis python.org (Downloads > macOS > « macOS 64-bit universal2 installer », version 3.13 ou 3.14), puis dans Terminal : python3 -m pip install pandas
steps.detail: Don't rely on /usr/bin/python3. From memory, it is a stub that asks to install the Xcode Command Line Tools and then gives Python 3.9.x. Confirmed from PyPI: pandas 3.x requires Python >= 3.11, so 3.9 would install pandas 2.3.3. This repo was tested here with Python 3.13 and pandas 3.0.5, so a 3.9 + 2.3 setup would be untested. python.org lists 3.14.10 and 3.13.17 (Oct 2026) universal2 installers; pandas 3.1.1 has macOS arm64 and x86_64 wheels. From memory: the python.org build is not marked 'externally managed', so pip works without a venv; afterwards run 'Install Certificates.command' from /Applications/Python 3.x. pont.py and releve.py parse as Python 3.9+ syntax (checked).

steps.action: Côté Claude (option recommandée) : installer l'appli Claude pour Mac, se connecter, créer un dossier vide ~/gold-orb (dans le dossier de départ, pas dans Documents ni Bureau), puis Réglages > Claude Code (ou Code) > activer « Use this computer from your phone and claude.ai » et y ajouter ~/gold-orb ; activer aussi « Keep this computer awake for Remote Control ». Laisser l'appli ouverte.
steps.detail: Per the docs: needs Claude Code v2.1.280 or later on the Mac, a Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise plan, and 'Require trusted devices' off. The task statement's menu name 'Remote Control' differs from the docs' 'Use this computer from your phone and claude.ai'; the label may vary. The lead then calls request_computer_folder and the user clicks Allow on the card. Once attached, the lead can itself write pont.py and the other files into ~/gold-orb, so the user never needs git. Alternative with no desktop app: in Terminal, run 'cd ~/gold-orb && claude remote-control' and leave it running.
steps.source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects.md (Run a thread on your own computer) ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control

steps.action: Plan B sans Remote Control : le responsable envoie ClaudeMains.mq5 et ReleveFP.mq5 (pièces jointes) ; l'utilisateur fait les étapes 8 à 13, puis ouvre …/MQL5/Files/claude dans le Finder et glisse le dossier « releve » (et account.txt, symbols.csv) dans la conversation claude.ai.
steps.detail: This needs no Python or Claude app on the Mac for the first session. It works for the survey (ReleveFP) and for checking that the EA exports data, but not for live brain operation, which needs a Python process on the Mac. Wait for fini.txt before copying the releve files.

pitfalls.risk: pont.py Hands.find() uses glob('~/Library/Application Support/**/MQL5/Files/claude', recursive=True). The MT5 Wine prefix contains dosdevices/c: -> ../drive_c and dosdevices/z: -> /. Python's recursive glob follows directory symlinks, so it would walk the entire disk through z: (and back into ~/Library through it, nesting until ELOOP). It finds the folder at least twice and can take a very long time. It can also trigger macOS privacy prompts for Desktop/Documents/Downloads, other apps' containers and removable volumes.
pitfalls.detect: 'python3 pont.py' hangs for minutes, the CPU or disk is busy, macOS privacy dialogs appear, or several paths come back for one terminal.
pitfalls.workaround: Don't let find() run on the Mac as it stands. Pass the folder explicitly (Hands(Path.home()/'Library/Application Support/net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5/drive_c/Program Files/MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Files/claude')), or have the owner change the pattern to a non-recursive '…/Application Support/*/drive_c/Program Files/*/MQL5/Files/claude'. pont.py is read-only for me.
pitfalls.source: Confirmed: Wine 11.7 ntdll.so in the 2026-10 installer contains 'dosdevices/c:' and 'dosdevices/z:' (strings); glob symlink-following and loop behaviour reproduced on Python 3.13 with a simulated prefix in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-gold-orb/340d9f5a-4d28-5733-90cb-10a10699d00b/scratchpad/veille/mac/globtest. That z: points to '/' is from memory (standard Wine).

pitfalls.risk: The official 'Installation on Mac OS' help page links an old installer (Feb 2025, Wine 10.0). Old Wine builds (8.x, 10.x) are reported to crash on recent macOS.
pitfalls.detect: The Journal startup line says 'on Wine 8.' or 'on Wine 10.'
pitfalls.workaround: Install from metatrader5.com/en/download (the metaquotes.ltd link, Wine 11.7). If an old install exists, delete the app and both prefix folders as the help page says, after backing up anything needed.
pitfalls.source: Confirmed by downloading both pkgs and reading their Distribution files and ntdll.so; https://www.mql5.com/en/forum/509934

pitfalls.risk: macOS Tahoe 26.5: several forum reports (May to July 2026) of MT5 closing unexpectedly, especially while opening or closing positions. That is exactly when ClaudeMains works. The reports involve Wine 8.0.1 and some recent builds; no fix was confirmed.
pitfalls.detect: The MT5 window disappears. Positions keep their broker-side stops (rule 1), but the EA's daily-loss, Friday-close and TTL logic stops.
pitfalls.workaround: Use the latest installer (Wine 11.x); for diagnosis, launch from Terminal with '/Applications/MetaTrader\ 5.app/Contents/MacOS/MetaTrader\ 5 > ~/mt5.log 2>&1' (MetaQuotes staff suggestion). Rely on the broker-side SL. Consider a Windows VPS later.

pitfalls.risk: File > Open Data Folder on the Mac opens a Wine Explorer window (or just beeps); pasting files there often fails.
pitfalls.detect: The user says 'nothing happens' or 'I can't paste'.
pitfalls.workaround: Use Finder > Go > Go to Folder with the full path from step 8. Some users report that dragging the .mq5 into MetaEditor's Navigator > Experts also works.

pitfalls.risk: Mac keyboard: F7 and F4 act as media keys, and the Wine windows use Ctrl shortcuts, not Cmd.
pitfalls.workaround: Use the menu items and toolbar buttons (Compile, Algo Trading), or press fn+F7.

pitfalls.risk: Sleep or a closed lid stops MT5, Python and Remote Control. Wine's Mac driver turns off App Nap but still allows idle system sleep.
pitfalls.detect: Gaps in bars_*.csv; the Claude thread shows the computer disconnected.
pitfalls.workaround: Step 2 settings, keep the lid open on power, and the Claude app's 'Keep this computer awake for Remote Control'.
pitfalls.source: winemac.so in the 2026 installer contains 'beginActivityWithOptions:reason:' / 'Running Windows program' (confirmed string; what options it passes is from memory of the Wine source); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects.md

pitfalls.risk: ReleveFP writes m1_*.csv, fiches.csv and tous.csv in place, with no tmp file and rename. As far as I know, Wine's share modes are enforced only between Wine processes and don't lock out a native macOS reader, so a native reader can see half-written files.
pitfalls.detect: A truncated last line in a CSV.
pitfalls.workaround: Read or copy the releve files only after fini.txt exists. ClaudeMains' exports use tmp + FileMove(FILE_REWRITE) and pont.py writes tmp + os.replace; on APFS os.replace is an atomic rename(2). From memory, Wine implements MoveFileEx(REPLACE_EXISTING) with rename(), and pont._read retries on FileNotFoundError anyway.

mac.files_path:
Confirmed (official help page; launcher strings 'net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5' and 'C:\Program Files\MetaTrader 5\terminal64.exe' in both the 2025 and 2026 installers; forum user report 2025-09; forum Journal line Aug 2026): ~/Library/Application Support/net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5/drive_c/Program Files/MetaTrader 5/ is both the install folder and the data folder. Hence:
- MQL5/Experts = ~/Library/Application Support/net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5/drive_c/Program Files/MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Experts
- MQL5/Scripts = …/MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Scripts
- MQL5/Files = …/MetaTrader 5/MQL5/Files, created on the first file write; ClaudeMains uses MQL5/Files/claude and ReleveFP uses MQL5/Files/claude/releve.
- EA logs: …/MQL5/Logs. Terminal logs: …/MetaTrader 5/Logs.
The bundle id is net.metaquotes.wine.MetaTrader5 and the prefix folder name is lowercase net.metaquotes.wine.metatrader5. An older layout was ~/Library/Application Support/MetaTrader 5/Bottles/metatrader5/drive_c/… (forum 2023); delete it if present. I found no FP-branded Mac build, so I can't say whether a branded build would use another prefix. The common folder (FILE_COMMON) would be under drive_c/users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/MetaQuotes/Terminal/Common/Files (from memory); the bridge doesn't use it.
How the user opens it: File > Open Data Folder exists but on the Mac opens a Wine Explorer window, and forum users say paste there often fails or the command beeps. Recommend instead Finder > Go > Go to Folder… (Shift-Cmd-G) and paste the full path; ~/Library is hidden in Finder, but Go to Folder reaches it. Copy .mq5 files in with Finder, then refresh the MetaEditor or MT5 Navigator.
mac.python_access:
Reading and writing: the MT5 app is not sandboxed (embedded entitlements: app-sandbox false, confirmed), so the prefix lives in plain ~/Library/Application Support and not in ~/Library/Containers. Apple's 'access data from other apps' prompt is tied to other apps' containers (Apple developer forum report). As far as I know, Application Support/net.metaquotes… is not a protected location, so a native python3 run from Terminal or by Claude should read and write there with no prompt. Not tested on a real Mac.
Locking: from memory, Wine enforces Windows share modes only inside wineserver, so a native process is never blocked by MT5 and MT5 is never blocked by Python. There is no protection against half-written reads either. The protocol depends on tmp-then-rename on both sides:
- pont._put writes <name>.tmp then os.replace, which is rename(2) and atomic on APFS within one volume.
- ClaudeMains writes .tmp then FileMove(FILE_REWRITE). From memory, Wine maps that to rename(); if it did delete-then-move instead, pont._read's retry on FileNotFoundError covers the gap.
- ReleveFP writes its CSVs in place (confirmed in the code), so read them only after fini.txt.
- A file renamed into cmd/ is visible at once to the EA's FileFindFirst('cmd\\*.txt'). '*.txt' won't match '*.txt.tmp' (from memory).
Which Python: install the python.org universal2 installer, 3.13 or 3.14 (python.org lists 3.14.10 and 3.13.17, Oct 2026), then run `python3 -m pip install pandas`, which today gives pandas 3.1.x (PyPI). Don't use /usr/bin/python3: from memory it is the Command Line Tools Python 3.9, and PyPI confirms pandas 3 needs Python 3.11 or later, so it would get pandas 2.3.3, an untested combination.
pont.py pattern: the folder it targets is right, but the recursive '**' pattern is dangerous on the Mac. The prefix's dosdevices/z: link (to '/') makes the glob walk the whole disk; I confirmed that z: is created by the bundled Wine and that glob follows symlinks. Use the explicit path or a non-recursive pattern (see pitfalls).
mac.remote_control:
From the docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects.md 'Run a thread on your own computer'; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control): a thread on the user's computer is a real Claude Code session running on the Mac in the shared folder. It uses the Mac's files, tools and Claude Code settings, including permission rules and hooks. It runs in auto mode when that is available, otherwise prompts wait in the thread. It needs Claude Code v2.1.280 or later, the desktop app open with 'Use this computer from your phone and claude.ai' on and the folder added (or 'claude remote-control' running in that folder), and 'Require trusted devices' off. It pauses while the Mac sleeps; there is a 'Keep this computer awake for Remote Control' switch. The rule that the home directory, hidden directories directly under it and ~/Library cannot be shared appears only in this session's tool description, not in the public docs. The same description says the feature 'is not available to everyone yet'.
Outside the folder, per permissions.md:
- File reads (Read/Grep) need no approval only inside the working directories; elsewhere they prompt, or the auto-mode classifier decides.
- Built-in read-only Bash commands (ls, cat, find, head…) run without a prompt even outside, unless permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories is set.
- Any other Bash command, such as `python3 pont.py`, needs approval or the auto-mode classifier. Once it runs, the Python process itself can read and write ~/Library, because Claude's rules govern tools, not child processes, and the sandbox is off by default.
- Symlinks: both the link path and the resolved path are checked. An allow rule must match both. A write through a symlinked directory that resolves outside the working directories is not auto-approved and prompts in auto mode. So a link ~/gold-orb/mt5 -> …/MQL5/Files/claude would work but keep prompting.
- permissions.additionalDirectories in ~/gold-orb/.claude/settings.local.json makes that path readable without prompts. Docs say such threads use the machine's settings, but I have not verified this for attached cloud sessions.
- On macOS, background sessions get separate privacy prompts for ~/Desktop, ~/Documents and ~/Downloads, so keep ~/gold-orb directly in home.
Recommended arrangement (fewest user steps): the user installs the Claude desktop app and signs in, creates an empty ~/gold-orb, turns on the switch and adds ~/gold-orb, and turns on keep-awake. The lead calls list_computer_folders, then request_computer_folder, and the user clicks Allow. The lead writes pont.py and the brain into ~/gold-orb itself and runs python3 with the explicit MT5 path. MT5 itself still has to be installed and the .mq5 files compiled and attached by hand: MetaEditor and chart attachment are GUI-only. Computer use could do that, but I didn't research it.
Alternative: run the brain in a session on the Mac (desktop app Code tab, or `cd ~/gold-orb && claude remote-control`). This is the same mechanism, but the user drives it.
Fallback with no Remote Control: the user receives the two .mq5 files, does steps 8 to 13 and drags the claude/releve folder plus account.txt and symbols.csv into the claude.ai chat. That covers the survey and export check, not live brain operation.
